Multicoin Says HYPE Is Its Hedge Fund's Largest Position, Stays With Crypto Over AI

According to Bloomberg, Multicoin Capital, which manages about $2.7 billion, plans to remain focused on crypto even as peers including Paradigm, Framework Ventures and Haun Ventures expand into AI. General partner Spencer Applebaum said HYPE is currently the largest position in Multicoin’s hedge fund and was acquired through the public market, though he did not disclose the size of the holding. He added that the firm sees no reason to shift away from crypto simply to follow the AI investment boom. — link

Hyperliquid Policy Center urges SEC to refine airdrop, secondary trading rules

Hyperliquid Policy Center submitted comments on the SEC’s proposed Regulation Crypto Assets, calling for clearer treatment of free token airdrops, broader secondary trading for exempt tokens, expanded safe harbors and clearer rules for token buybacks. The SEC proposal includes exemptions for startup token offerings of up to $5 million over four years and qualifying fundraising of up to $75 million in any 12-month period. — link

Metaplanet nears US takeover as Super League shareholders approve 2,100 BTC deal

Super League shareholders approved Metaplanet’s planned investment, including the issuance of shares and warrants and the rebranding to Superplanet. At closing, Metaplanet is expected to contribute 2,100 BTC and $2.5 million in cash and would own about 93.7% of the company’s common stock. Superplanet is intended to serve as Metaplanet’s U.S.-listed Bitcoin treasury platform, while related warrants could provide up to roughly $3.4 billion in additional equity capital. — link

BitMine Adds 12,535 ETH, Total Holdings Reach 6.04M ETH

BitMine said it acquired 12,535 ETH over the past week, bringing total holdings to 6,041,481 ETH, or about 4.9% of Ethereum’s 122.1 million supply. The company has 5.07 million ETH staked, while its total crypto, cash, marketable securities and other investments were valued at $15.1 billion as of October 18. — link

Strategy expands buyback to $3B, buys 267 BTC

Strategy said it acquired 267 BTC for $22.1 million at an average price of $82,900 between October 12 and 18, bringing total holdings to 848,517 BTC. The company also repurchased 1.94 million STRC shares for $193.1 million and increased its digital credit securities repurchase authorization from $2 billion to $3 billion, leaving $1.16 billion available. The bitcoin purchase was funded mainly through $22 million in MSTR share sales.

Strive CEO Matt Cole said the company purchased 1,223 BTC between Wednesday and Friday at an average price of $81,73

BNB Chain burns 1.65M BNB worth about $1B in 37th quarterly auto-burn

BNB Chain completed its 37th quarterly BNB Auto-Burn, removing about 1.646 million BNB worth roughly $1 billion at the reference price. The Auto-Burn mechanism determines the amount based on BNB’s price and the number of BNB Smart Chain blocks produced during the quarter, with the long-term goal of reducing total BNB supply to 100 million. BNB Chain also continues to burn a portion of gas fees through BEP-95. — link

JPMorgan to Offer JPM Coin Deposit Token to Institutional Clients on Ethereum

According to Bloomberg, JPMorgan announced that it will offer its JPM Coin deposit token to institutional clients on Ethereum, enabling round-the-clock payments that settle in seconds. The token represents clients’ U.S. dollar deposits at JPMorgan and first launched on Base last year. It is expected to support on-chain payments for large clients in the crypto sector, as well as settlement or collateralization of tokenized asset transactions by financial institutions. — link

Vitalik: EIP-8288 Enables Arbitrary Signature Schemes, Ethereum May Never Need New Precompiles

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin said the ideal way to support everyone’s cryptography is through EIP-8288: users can generate any signature scheme locally, prove it with a STARK, and have it included via a stark aggregator, without putting calldata on-chain. This would allow Ethereum to never add a new precompile again.

He added that Lattice schemes could still be supported via precompiles for accounts and wallets if proven AI-secure. — link
